name: Cooperative
scope: The cooperative movement as its defining sources present it (s1 ICA Statement on the Cooperative Identity, s2-s3 Britannica, s4 Webb, s5 Gide, s6 Holyoake): the idea that people should meet their economic, social and cultural needs through jointly owned, democratically controlled enterprises of their members (one member, one vote, limited return on capital, surpluses shared by use, open voluntary membership, autonomy, education, cooperation among cooperatives, concern for community), from the Rochdale Pioneers of 1844 and the British, French and German cooperative tradition (Holyoake, Gide) to the ICA's 1995 statement. Covers consumer, producer/worker, credit and agricultural cooperation as one movement. Excludes Owenism (Robert Owen is reserved for it), the wider socialisms and mutualism that sources only relate to cooperatives, and cooperatives as mere business forms with no stated ideas, and what individual co-op businesses do commercially.

summary: The cooperative movement holds that people should meet their economic, social and cultural needs through enterprises they jointly own and democratically control as members: open voluntary membership, one member one vote, limited return on capital, surpluses shared by use, autonomy, education and cooperation among cooperatives. Its classic consumer branch (Rochdale 1844, Holyoake, Gide) aims to replace profit-seeking with service of needs by an evolutionary, non-revolutionary route.
